'''''Tetrapanax papyrifer''''', the '''rice paper plant''' (通草—''tong cao''), is an [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Araliaceae]], the [[monotypic genus|sole species]] in the [[genus]] '''''Tetrapanax'''''.<ref name="POWO">{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |author-link1=Plants of the World Online |id=86417-3 |title=''Tetrapanax papyrifer'' (Hook.) K.Koch |access-date=29 June 2024 }}</ref><ref name="efloras">{{cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=132603 |title=''Tetrapanax'' |author=Qibai Xiang & Porter P. Lowry |work=Flora of China |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden, St. Louis, MO & Harvard University Herbaria, Cambridge, MA |access-date=16 July 2014}}</ref> The [[specific name (botany)|specific epithet]] is frequently misspelled as "papyriferum", "papyriferus", or "papyrifera". It is [[native plant|native]] to eastern and central [[China]] and [[Taiwan]],<ref name="POWO" /> but widely [[Horticulture|cultivated]] in [[East Asia]] and in other [[tropical]]<ref>George W. Staples and Derral R. Herbst. 2005. "A Tropical Garden Flora". Bishop Museum Press: Honolulu, HI, USA.</ref> to mild [[temperate climate|temperate]] regions as well.<ref name = RHSPF/><ref>{{PLANTS|id=TEPA3|taxon=Tetrapanax papyrifer|accessdate=9 December 2015}}</ref>

The species was first described in the genus ''[[Aralia]]'' as ''Aralia papyrifera'', and has also been treated in ''[[Fatsia]]'' as ''Fatsia papyrifera''.<ref name="POWO" /><ref name=FoC>{{cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200015315 |title=''Tetrapanax papyrifer'' |author=Qibai Xiang & Porter P. Lowry |work=Flora of China |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden, St. Louis, MO & Harvard University Herbaria, Cambridge, MA |access-date=16 July 2014}}</ref>

A second species, ''Tetrapanax tibetanus'', is now regarded as a synonym of ''[[Merrilliopanax alpinus]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=250073383 |title=''Merrilliopanax alpinus'' |author=Qibai Xiang & Porter P. Lowry |work=Flora of China |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden, St. Louis, MO & Harvard University Herbaria, Cambridge, MA |access-date=16 July 2014}}</ref>

==Description==
''Tetrapanax'' grows between 3–7 metres tall, with usually unbranched stems 2–9 cm in diameter, and bearing a rosette of large [[leaf|leaves]] atop the crown; the top of the plant can visually, albeit superficially, appear similar to a number of plants belonging to ''[[Arecaceae]]'' (the palm family). The leaves are carried on 40–60 cm petioles; the orbicular leaf blade measures from 50 to 75 cm across (to a metre across in some cultivars<ref name="Rex" />), with anywhere from 5-12 deeply incised palmate lobes, the central lobes being larger and Y-forked near the end. It spreads extensively, by sprouts and runners from the [[root]] system, underground. The [[inflorescence]] is a large [[panicle]] of hemispherical or globular [[umbel]]s, at the end of the stem. The [[flowers]] have 4-6 small, white petals. The [[fruit]] is a small [[berry]] 4 mm in diameter.<ref name="FoC" />

==Uses==
=== Paper ===
{{main|Pith paper}}
The [[pith]] of ''Tetrapanax papyrifer'' is traditionally used to make paper. First, the boughs are boiled and freed from bark. The cylindrical core of pith is rolled on a hard flat surface against a knife, by which it is cut into thin sheets of a fine ivory-like texture.<ref name=TP>{{citation |journal=探索·发现 |year=2011 |number=139 |title=通草奇画 |url=http://kejiao.cntv.cn/history/tansuofaxian/classpage/video/20110519/101220.shtml |publisher=CCTV}}</ref><ref name=FoC/>

The paper was used extensively in late 19th century [[Guangdong]] as a common support medium for [[gouache]] paintings sold to Western clients. The paper was colloquially thought by Europeans to be '[[Rice paper (disambiguation)|rice paper]]'. The term was first defined in the Chinese–English Dictionary of [[Robert Morrison (missionary)|Robert Morrison]] who referred to the use of the Chinese medicinal plant as material for painting, as well as for making [[artificial flowers]] and [[Sole (shoe)|shoe soles]].<ref name=TP/>

Dyed in various colours, this rice paper is extensively used for the preparation of artificial flowers, while the white sheets are employed for [[watercolor]] drawings. Due to its texture, this paper is not suited for writing.{{Citation needed|date=March 2009}}

=== Other uses ===
''Tetrapanax papyrifer'' is used in [[traditional Chinese medicine]].<ref name=FoC/>

The species is cultivated as an ornamental specimen plant, and has received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/18051/Tetrapanax-papyrifer/Details | title = ''Tetrapanax papyrifer'' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 4 June 2021}}</ref>

==Cultivars==
The [[cultivar]] 'Rex' is a semi-evergreen shrub or tree with huge palmate leaves up to a metre diameter. Classified by the Royal Horticultural Society as H4, it is evergreen in mild locations, [[deciduous]] where temperatures fall below freezing, and [[herbaceous]] with more prolonged freezing. It prefers a sheltered position in full sun or partial shade.<ref name="Rex">{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/191283/Tetrapanax-papyrifer-Rex/Details | title = ''Tetrapanax papyrifer'' 'Rex' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 4 June 2021}}</ref>
